# #443 — Open Brain is the memory: canon loads itself, and nobody re-explains how we work

State: OPEN
Author: rodaddy
Labels: wayfinder:map
Created: 2026-07-29T19:20:32Z
Updated: 2026-07-30T01:23:07Z

## Destination

**A session starts and the rules are already there.** Canon — who Rico is, how
work is done, this repo's facts — loads automatically and correctly every time,
process knowledge is reachable without being told to go look, and capture
records both sides of the work so the next session inherits what this one
learned. Reached when Rico can start cold and re-explain nothing.

**Claude first, then adapters for Claudex, Codex, and Pi** — and only where
Claude's fit does not transfer exactly. The adapter delta is itself a signal: if
the contract has to bend per runtime, the contract is wrong, not the runtime.
Settled 2026-07-29. A memory contract four harnesses depend on is far harder to
change once they are all wired to it, and #445 (how canon is written) and #447
(whether capture distills) are still open — getting those wrong in one runtime
is a fix, in four it is a migration.

**Why this outranks DREAM, in Rico's terms:** dreaming becomes much more
straightforward afterward, because there is more data to train from. REM
currently grades a corpus of Rico's prompts with none of the agent's reasoning
in it (#447). Fix capture and the same pipeline has both sides. Canon-first is
not just dependency order — it is what makes DREAM cheap later.

## Notes

**Domain:** Open Brain as a first-class memory substrate, not a skill you invoke.

**This map carries execution.** Wayfinder plans by default; this effort
overrides that. The destination is a change in place — memory actually firing —
so tickets that build and wire are in scope. A plan that leaves canon empty and
nothing loading is not the destination.

**Standing model (settled 2026-07-29, do not relitigate):**
- Canon auto-loads: user, soul (rules + process), repo facts. Everything else,
  including episodic lane history, is explicit-on-request — auto-loading it
  contaminates unrelated work and forecloses a deliberate fresh start.
- Canon carries the short absolute RULE; the index serves the full procedure on
  trigger. Front-of-mind works because it is small.
- Skills stay in files (git, diffs, review); OB/qmd index them in place.
- Endpoints come from `$OPENBRAIN_BASE_URL`. Never hardcode a host.
- Persona *voice* switching is parked deliberately — `ACTIVE_PERSONA=bob` is
  stale by choice, not broken. Persona as a *thinking lens* (adversary,
  maintainer, skeptic; possibly routed to another harness) is a separate and
  open question — see the lens ticket. Do not revive voice switching here.
- **Memory calls are enforced, not remembered.** "First-class" means the harness
  requires the call; an agent that *can* use memory and one that *cannot skip it*
  behave completely differently. Precedent lives in this repo:
  `.claude/hooks/design-lookup-gate.ts`.

**Skills to consult:** `_ob/skills/brain/workflows/canon.md` (the model),
`_ob/skills/brain/workflows/resume.md`, `_ob/skills/skill-maintainer/` before
touching any skill.

**Design doc:** `_plans/canon-always-known.md` — measurements, rationale, and
what was already rejected.

**Out of scope, explicitly:** DREAM (Light/REM/Deep). Useful later; canon is its
consumer and must work first.

## Decisions so far

<!-- one line per closed ticket: enough to judge relevance, then zoom the link -->

- [How does anything get INTO canon?](https://github.com/rodaddy/open-brain/issues/445) — two write paths already exist. Guidance lanes: an `ob_session_events` row with `metadata.candidate_type` = `user_preference`/`process_rule` **plus** `memory_lifecycle_action='promote'`. Repo facts: `upsert_repo_fact` into `ob_entities`, bound to the active repo exactly. Canon is empty because **nothing was ever promoted** — the DB holds exactly one `user_preference` and one `process_rule`, both still `candidate`, and 13 `repo_fact` rows, none for open-brain. Authority is metadata, **not** tier (hot/warm/cold is decay, a separate model). Retirement is a newer `relegate`/`discard` on the same `candidate_scope.key` — **so every seeded rule must carry a scope key or it can never be cleanly retired**.
- [Fleet index is 20% third-party code, and buzz's checkout is dirty](https://github.com/rodaddy/open-brain/issues/449) — resolved outside the map. Prior art lives outside the working tree in a per-repo `ref-<repo>` named index, sources never written to; `buzz` is out of Development and `ai-agents` owns it via `ref-ai-agents`. Two working examples now, which closes the original gap: with only open-brain doing it right, there was no pattern to copy.

## Not yet specified

- **Who decides what gets promoted, and when.** #445 settled the *mechanism*
  (lifecycle promote + `candidate_scope.key`); what remains is the policy — does
  an agent propose a candidate and Rico promotes, does DREAM propose, or is
  promotion always manual. Sharpens once the seed exists and something has
  actually needed retiring.
- **What "front of mind" costs in practice.** The budget for the always-loaded
  set is unmeasured. Cannot be sized until something actually loads.
- **Whether capture should distill or store raw.** The standing rule says never
  raw transcripts; the automatic path stores raw prompts. Whether the fix is a
  distillation step, a different write path, or a policy change is open.
- **How other repos inherit this.** Rules proven here get forced into other
  repos ("when things work in here I force them into other repos"), mechanism
  unspecified.
- **Skill/capability discovery beyond the policy index.** Vectorizing skills in
  place is agreed in principle; the retrieval shape and whether it is qmd or OB
  is not settled.
- **qmd cache hygiene** (residue from #449, too small to ticket): `fleet.sqlite`
  still holds `buzz` (2,205 of 11,486) because it was not rebuilt after the move,
  so `aqmd all` still ranks it. Superseded index files also remain on disk —
  `research.sqlite` duplicates `ref-open-brain.sqlite`, and
  `ai-agents-research.sqlite` duplicates `ref-ai-agents.sqlite`. Caches are
  expendable; a scoped rebuild and a delete clear both. Likely folds into #448.
